reconcile.connective: Keil & Delitzsch treat 'eight hundred' as original and argue Chronicles' 'three hundred' crept in from Abishai's nearby tally.

discrepancy.connective: Steve Wells's Skeptic's Annotated Bible presses the plain numbers: the same feat is eight hundred kills in one book, three hundred in the other.

skeptic.name: Steve Wells
skeptic.attribution: Steve Wells, The Skeptic's Annotated Bible (skepticsannotatedbible.com, 1999; print ed. 2013)

excerpts.excerpt_text: "He swung his spear over eight hundred slain at once." This is not to be understood as signifying that he killed eight hundred men at one blow, but that in a battle he threw his spear again and again at the foe, until eight hundred men had been slain. The Chronicles give three hundred instead of eight hundred; and as that number occurs again in Sa2 23:18, in the case of Abishai, it probably found its way from that verse into this in the book of Chronicles.
excerpts.on_tension_rationale: Directly addresses the 800-vs-300 numeral gap between 2 Sam 23:8 and 1 Chr 11:11 with a text-critical harmonization: 'eight hundred' is the original figure, and Chronicles' 'three hundred' is explained as scribal contamination from the nearby Abishai tally (2 Sam 23:18), so the two texts are not reporting genuinely different facts.

pd_work.resource: John Haley, An Examination of the Alleged Discrepancies of the Bible (1874)
pd_work.author: John Haley
pd_work.note: Haley treats this exact pair of verses (2 Sam 23:8 / 1 Chr 11:11) under 'Historical Discrepancies,' concluding on the authority of Hervey, Keil, Kennicott, and Gesenius that the original text read 'eight hundred' and that 'Adino the Eznite' is itself a corrupted rendering of 'he swung his spear.'
